violation_type.title: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device - Remove the infant from the device and place the infant in a crib as soon as possible (26 TAC §746.2426(a)(2))
violation_type.short_title: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device - Remove the infant from the device and place the infant in a crib as soon as possible
violation_type.typical_finding: Based on the information obtained during the investigation, it was determined that a caregiver allowed an infant to fall asleep in a restrictive device (swing) for approximately twelve minutes before removing the infant from the device and placing the infant in a crib.

finding_variants.text: Based on the information obtained during the investigation, it was determined that a caregiver allowed an infant to fall asleep in a restrictive device (swing) for approximately twelve minutes before removing the infant from the device and placing the infant in a crib.
During the investigation process, an infant fell asleep in a restrictive device and was not moved to a crib.

CCR observed an infant under 12 months strapped in a baby swing, sleeping in the restrictive device. The infant caregiver confirmed that the infant had been sleeping in the device for 10 minutes.    Correction made: The infant caregiver removed the infant from the restrictive device.
An 11 month old infant was observed asleep on a bouncer. The infant was observed with a bottle and covered with a blanket.
During a walk through of the building, it was observed two infants ages 17 months and 7 months sleeping in restrictive devices. This was corrected at inspection.
This investigation was part of an Abuse Neglect investigation.  During the inspection a 14-month-old infant was observed sleeping in a swing.
